regions.barrier: THE CAMPUS GATE (rows 1-2). A run of `cliff` tiles across cols 0-3 and cols 9-33 at rows 1-2, with a 3-tile opening at cols 5-7 where the road passes. A `lamp` decor at [4,2] and [8,2] as the piers. Above it, rows 0-1, a solid conifer band (see vegetation) so the map's top edge is closed forest and the first thing the walker does is pass THROUGH something. This is the only barrier that is not crossed on entry from a previous region — it is the opening frame.
regions.landmark: The BIT academic block: 10 tiles wide x 7 tall (cols 10-19, rows 6-12). Nothing else in the region exceeds 6 tiles in either dimension. Its front row (12) sits directly on the north edge of the quad, so the walker turning east at [6,17] has the full 160px façade above him for the whole 14-tile leg. Use plaster-and-beam walls + the wide brown wood roof from pc/roofs.webp.

(1) Top forest band rows 0-3, every col except 4-8: `tree` where c%2==0 and r in {0,2}, `treeSmall` where c%2==1 and r in {1,3} — a wall of canopy. (2) Grove NE cols 24-33, rows 4-14, fill 0.55 via a hash (e.g. (c*7+r*13)%100<55) with min spacing 2 — this backs the academic block so its roof reads against dark canopy. (3) Grove W cols 0-4, rows 14-21, fill 0.45, tying the hostel block into the map edge. (4) Forest corridor rows 18-22: cols 0-11 and 24-33 at fill 0.60, cols 12-23 at 0.15 — this is the travel stretch, and it must be closed on both sides so the town clearing below reads as arrival. INSIDE the town clearing (cols 8-27, rows 22-36) place exactly ONE tree, at [21,24], the village tree; zero others. Margin trees only at cols 0-7 and 28-33 for rows 23-36, fill 0.35. Rows 36-38: no trees at all, `reeds` at row 37 every 3rd col — the ground going soft before the river.

regions.barrier: THE RIVER GORGE AND BRIDGE. Water blob rows 38-40, cols 0-33 (full width, no way round it), with `cliff` bank tiles at row 37 and row 41 except where the bridge lands. The `bridge` sheet at cols 12-14, rows 37-41. Then, a beat later, THE CITY WALL: `cliff` run at rows 43-44 across cols 0-11 and cols 15-33, gate opening cols 12-14, `lamp` at [11,44] and [15,44]. Two things crossed in eight rows is what makes the capital feel entered rather than reached.
regions.landmark: The wall tower: 4 wide x 11 tall (cols 29-32, rows 42-52). Delhi's landmark is dominant by HEIGHT, not spread — the only vertical on the map. Its base sits on the wall line (rows 43-44) so it reads as a gate/watch tower, and its top overhangs the river bank. Blue slate roof, brick walls.
regions.vegetation: ZERO trees inside the wall (rows 44-60). That absence is the whole point — it is what makes the region read as paved. Instead: (1) Riverbank willows, `treeSmall` only, rows 41-42, at cols 0,3,6,9 and 16,19,22,25,28,31 — a thin regular line, not a mass. (2) Green belt south of the plaza, rows 61-64, cols 0-7 and 26-33, fill 0.40 — the periphery. (3) Farm blobs at cols 0-8 rows 61-64 and cols 26-33 rows 61-64, wheat decor inside. (4) Inside the wall the only planting is `potRed`/`potYellow` at each building's front row, two per building at footprint x+1 and x+w-2, plus `lamp` at the plaza corners [2,59], [31,59], [2,52], [31,52] and flanking the gate street mouth at [11,51], [15,51].

clusters.shape: A walled square with a continuous north frontage — the only cluster on the map where buildings touch each other. The PLAZA is a `path` blob cols 2-31, rows 51-60, minus footprints. The GATE STREET is a `path` rect cols 12-14, rows 44-51, running from the wall gate down into the plaza; jaiswal and the civic hall face each other across it. Reading the north frontage west to east: terrace (1-3), jaiswal (5-10), street (12-14), civic hall (16-20), then medicfibers set forward into the plaza (22-27) and the tower closing the north-east (29-32). Market stalls along the plaza's south edge, rows 59-60, cols 6-20 — `fences` run plus alternating potRed/potYellow/wheat crates — so the square is enclosed on four sides without a building turning its back on it. The road's east-west leg at row 56 crosses the plaza's lower half; the walker sees every façade above him.

globalNotes:
ANCHOR CONVENTION. Every `col`,`row` above is a BOTTOM-LEFT anchor in tiles, matching Scene.sprite(name, cx, cy) which places a sprite at cy*TILE - h + TILE. So a building with col=10, row=12, footprint [10,7] occupies cols 10..19 and rows 6..12, with row 12 being its front (façade) row. All footprints are the full drawn bounding box including roof overhang, not just the wall.

THE FACING RULE, AND WHY EVERYTHING IS "SOUTH". Cute Fantasy and the Pixel Crawler wall/roof parts only draw a front elevation facing the bottom of the screen. So "doors face the approach" (HANDOFF 9.9 rule 3) resolves to a hard geometric constraint: every shared space must lie SOUTH of the buildings that front it. Buildings therefore range along a yard's NORTH edge, or sit flush to its east/west edge with their front row level with the yard's bottom row. Nothing is ever placed directly south of a yard facing away from it — where a cluster needs a fourth side, it is closed with fences, market stalls or a decor run, never a building's back. The walker moves top-to-bottom throughout, so this also means he sees a façade the entire time he is inside a cluster.

BAND CHANGES — I am proposing new bands, and PATH/STOPS[].at must be recomputed. New REGIONS rows: mesra [0,38], delhi [38,64], ranchi [64,80], dhahran [86,104], with the sea occupying 80-86 (SEA = { row: 80, height: 6 }). Reasons: (a) mesra now carries TWO clusters — the BIT campus and the Ranchi town where Chadda and Metarch1 actually were — plus a closed forest travel stretch between them, and 34 rows could not hold that; (b) old ranchi at 12 rows could not fit an 8x6 studio plus a yard plus fields, and it butted straight into the sea with no shore; (c) old dhahran got 28 rows for one building while delhi got 24 for a city — reversed. Also set delhi fields:0 (a walled capital has no farmland inside it; the two farm blobs are outside, rows 61-64) and raise ranchi fields to 0.55.

NEW PATH (axis-aligned, replaces the current one):
  [6,0], [6,17], [20,17], [20,26], [13,26], [13,56], [24,56], [24,76], [13,76], [13,102], [23,102]
Segment lengths / cumulative starts: 17/0, 14/17, 9/31, 7/40, 30/47, 11/77, 20/88, 11/108, 26/119, 10/145. PATH_LENGTH = 155. Two bends per region maximum; the long col-13 run (rows 26-56) is what carries the river crossing and the city gate without a zigzag.

NEW STOPS[].at (verified against the segments above, each landing level with its building's front or forecourt):
  barch 25, chadda 45, metarch1 56, jaiswal 72, medicfibers 88, metarch2 114, kfupm 150.
Minimum separation is 11 tiles (chadda→metarch1), so no two arrival cards can be on screen at once. Add a non-card beat at d≈2 for the campus gate if the banner system wants one.

STOPS[].side IS NOW WRONG AND SHOULD BE DROPPED. stopAnchor() derives a building position from pointAt(stop.at) + side*6, which is precisely the mechanism that produced the scatter — it can only make beads. Replace it with an explicit `anchor: [col,row]` and `footprint: [w,h]` per stop, taken from the tables above, and let the arrival card position itself from the building's bounding box (centre-x of the footprint, top edge minus 1 tile) rather than from `side`.

pathCells() STILL WORKS but is no longer sufficient. Keep it for the 3-wide spine, then union it with the explicit paved rects, which are what make the road serve the settlements (rule 2):
  quad          cols 9-21,  rows 13-18
  hostel apron  cols 0-7,   rows 13-15
  town apron    cols 12-21, rows 25-27
  forecourt     cols 15-21, rows 34-36  + spur cols 13-15, row 35
  gate street   cols 12-14, rows 44-51
  delhi plaza   cols 2-31,  rows 51-60
  ranchi yard   cols 12-25, rows 72-77  + barn spur cols 11-12, rows 76-77
  kfupm plaza   cols 4-33,  rows 100-104
Plus the 1-2 tile door spurs listed per cluster. Blob the union in one pass so the nine-slice gives the plazas real edges; subtract building footprints first or the roofs will sit on path tiles at their eaves.

DENSITY RHYTHM (rule 4), stated as row bands so it can be asserted in code. Dense (a cluster): rows 6-18, 22-36, 44-60, 66-77, 91-104. Open (travel): rows 0-5, 19-21, 37-43, 61-65, 78-90. No building anchor may fall in an open band, and tree fill in an open band must be either >0.5 (closed forest) or <0.1 (bare) — never the 0.2-0.4 middle, which is what reads as uniform scatter.

VEGETATION MUST BE HASHED, NOT rnd(). The current loop calls rnd() per attempted placement over a whole region, which is the definition of uniform scatter. Replace with per-mass fill: for each named rectangle above, iterate its cells and place where ((c*73856093) ^ (r*19349663)) % 100 < fill*100, rejecting any cell within 2 tiles of an already-placed `tree` (the 64x80 sprite is 4x5 tiles, so closer than 2 means overlap, not a grove). Every tree on the map belongs to exactly one named mass.

Y-SORT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THIS LAYOUT (HANDOFF 9.6 item 4). The NE grove at cols 24-33 rows 4-14 is specified to overlap the academic block's east eaves, and the conifer line at rows 64-66 to overlap metarch2's roof ridge — that overlap is what binds the layers (rule 8). Without sorting ops by (y + height) before render those canopies will draw behind the roofs and the whole scheme flattens.

BUILDING VOCABULARY, so the seven read as seven institutions (extends the 9.6 item-1 suggestion with the sizes settled here):
  barch       10x7  plaster-and-beam walls, wide brown wood roof   — the academic block
  chadda       4x4  dark log walls, brown wood roof                — the smallest thing on the map
  metarch1     5x5  plank/timber walls, green shingle roof
  jaiswal      6x7  brick walls, blue slate roof                   — tallest of the two Delhi offices
  medicfibers  6x6  glazed storefront, blue slate roof             — the only shopfront
  metarch2     8x6  plank/timber walls, green shingle roof         — metarch1's exact vocabulary, grown
  kfupm       12x8  white/pale plaster, flat pale roof             — no shingle anywhere on it
The metarch1 → metarch2 pairing is deliberate: identical materials, footprint up from 25 to 48 tiles. The return reads as a return without a label.

FILLER BUILDINGS. Ids prefixed `_` (_hostel, _workshop, _teahouse, _shed, _terrace, _civic, _tower, _annexe, _barn, _gatehouse, _wing_w, _wing_e) carry no card and no `at`. They exist because a cluster needs buildings that are not events — eleven of them against seven stops is roughly the ratio ref-1 and ref-5 run at, and it is the single biggest difference between a place and a menu.
